To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of text features on top of audio features is beneficial for the classification task of music genres.

(1) the combination of audio and textual features is beneficial for genre classification, (2) the combination of different types of textual features (content words and metadata) is beneficial for genre recognition, and (3) the combination of content words and low level audio features (MFCC, chroma) is beneficial for music genre classification, while the combination of content and high level features (timbre, rhythm) is less effective.
the combination of audio features and text features based on content terms is superior to the usage of either audio features or text features alone for genre classification.

the integration of text and audio features for music information retrieval.
the question: How can we integrate text and audio feature information for music information retrieval?
the combination of text and audio features for music classification.

the use of text and audio features in combination can be beneficial for the task of genre classification.

text features can be used as an enhancement to audio features for genre classification.

the combination of textual and audio features improves the classification accuracy for the task of genre classification in MIR.

the combination of textual data and audio features can be beneficial for genre classification in music information retrieval.

the combination of text features and audio features outperforms the individual modalities.
